title: Air India Deploys New Boeing 787-9 on Toronto Route, Launches Mumbai Service
excerpt: Airline eliminates Vienna fuel stop, restores daily Delhi-Toronto flights, and announces seasonal Mumbai-Toronto non-stop service starting October 2026.
body:
• Air India has deployed its factory-fresh Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi-Toronto route from August 1, eliminating the Vienna refuelling stop and cutting journey time by nearly three hours.
  • A new seasonal Mumbai-Toronto non-stop service will launch October 25, 2026, operating three times weekly — the first-ever direct link between the two cities by Air India.
  • The new aircraft brings Air India's redesigned three-class cabin to Canada for the first time, including Premium Economy and fully enclosed Business Class suites.

Air India has begun operating its newest Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi-Toronto route, eliminating a months-long refuelling stop in Vienna and restoring non-stop westbound flights from August 1. The airline simultaneously announced a new seasonal Mumbai-Toronto non-stop service launching October 25, marking a substantial expansion of its Canada operations.

The changes come as Air India also restores daily frequency on the Delhi-Toronto route after temporarily reducing service to five weekly flights during June and July due to elevated fuel costs and geopolitical disruptions.

Why the Vienna Stop Existed — and How the 787-9 Ends It

Pakistan's continued closure of its airspace to Indian-operated carriers has forced Air India to fly longer westbound routes over Europe. The diversions increased fuel consumption on the Delhi-Toronto sector to the point where the airline's Boeing 777-300ER could not complete the journey without a technical halt in Vienna.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-56NLCryCag

The Boeing 787-9, designed for long-range operations with a maximum range of roughly 8,300 nautical miles, allows Air India to fly the longer routing non-stop — subject to available airspace conditions. Journey time on flight AI187 drops from approximately 20 hours, including the fuel stop, to around 17 hours. The return flight, AI188, continues to operate non-stop at roughly 16 hours.

"Canada is home to one of the world's largest and most vibrant Indian diaspora communities, and Toronto has long been one of Air India's most important international gateways. As we continue transforming Air India into a world-class global airline, we are steadily expanding the availability of our newest aircraft and latest cabin products across key international routes."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO and Managing Director, Air India

A Three-Class Cabin Canada Has Not Seen Before

The aircraft assigned to Toronto is one of Air India's line-fit 787-9s — meaning its cabin was designed for the airline and installed at Boeing's production facility, not retrofitted onto an older frame. Air India received its first purpose-built 787-9, registered VT-AWA, in January 2026. It entered commercial service on the Mumbai-Frankfurt route in February.

The Toronto aircraft is configured with 296 seats across three cabins: 30 in Business Class, 28 in Premium Economy and 238 in Economy. Premium Economy is available on the India-Canada corridor for the first time.

Business Class features a 1-2-1 layout with fully enclosed suites, direct aisle access, 79-inch fully flat beds and 17-inch 4K QLED HDR entertainment screens. Premium Economy seats are arranged in a 2-3-2 configuration with 38 inches of pitch, adjustable leg rests and 13.3-inch screens. Economy receives redesigned seats with 11.6-inch 4K displays. All cabins use the Thales AVANT Up entertainment system with over 3,000 hours of content, Bluetooth audio connectivity and USB-A, USB-C and AC power.

Mumbai-Toronto Opens a New Gateway

The new Mumbai-Toronto service, launching October 25, will operate three times weekly during the Winter 2026 schedule. It will be operated by Boeing 777-300ER aircraft featuring First Class, Business and Economy cabins — making it one of the few Air India routes to offer a first-class product.

The route gives passengers from western and southern India a direct connection to Canada's largest city without routing through Delhi or connecting via European or Gulf carriers. Air India says the new service will add nearly 2,000 weekly seats on India-Canada routes.

"The launch of our seasonal Mumbai-Toronto service this Winter will provide travellers more choice and convenience at a time when many are travelling to reunite with family and friends."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

For the large Indian diaspora population across the Greater Toronto Area — many of whom have family roots in Mumbai, Gujarat and Maharashtra — the new direct service eliminates what has long been a cumbersome connection through Delhi or a transit through the Middle East. Students, families visiting relatives over the winter holidays, and business travellers between India's financial capital and Canada will benefit most directly.

What's Next

Air India's remaining three-times-weekly Delhi-Toronto services, currently operated by 777-300ER aircraft, are scheduled to transition to the new Boeing 787-9 from January 2027 as more aircraft join the fleet. The airline also maintains a Delhi-Vancouver service, currently operating five times weekly.

More than two million people travel between India and Canada annually, according to Air India. An interline agreement with WestJet allows passengers arriving in Toronto or Vancouver to connect onward to 17 Canadian and 14 U.S. destinations on a single ticket. With diplomatic relations between India and Canada still navigating turbulence, passenger demand has remained resilient — driven by family travel, student movements and growing business ties.
nri_angle: New Mumbai-Toronto direct service and upgraded Delhi-Toronto flights give the large Indian diaspora in Canada faster, more convenient travel options to India.
author: Diaspora Desk
